cases.title: A first-party native Driver and a community Driver on the real worker commit their Event through the same pass with the same authority outcome, and Local equals Air-Gapped
In one registry both Drivers commit in one batch in host schedule order, whichever isolation class is registered first

A first-party Driver and a community Driver on the real worker that propose another Plugin's Event type are refused with the same typed authority error, commit nothing and quarantine no Plugin; a first-party proposal of a reserved host type is refused too

An Event type has one owner whichever isolation class claims it first: a community claim on a first-party type, a first-party claim on a community type and either class's claim on a reserved consent type are refused alike before the registry changes

A Driver of either isolation class that fails while it stages, a community guest trap on the real worker or a first-party Driver failure, discards the whole scheduled pass including the other class's staged output, leaves the sibling available, quarantines only the trapping community Plugin, and the next pass commits

expected.community-fails.refusal: CommunityPlugin(ComponentTrap) host=ComponentTrap { class: Unreachable, reproduction: Unverified }

cases.title: A failing community Driver launches exactly one worker and is never replaced by a registered first-party Plugin with the same domain contract; a quarantined Plugin refuses the whole pass, and recovery is a new pass under new invocation identities, which the context source issues and this case models, that never reuses the failed output

expected.failed.refusal: CommunityPlugin(ComponentTrap) host=ComponentTrap { class: Unreachable, reproduction: Unverified }

cases.title: A required but unregistered Plugin of either isolation class fails exact resolution with the same MissingImplementation (a resolver-level parity), and a community member without an active release is refused at the trust gate before any Driver runs

An unavailable Plugin of either isolation class, marked by the host or quarantined through an injected host refusal, refuses the whole pass with the same ImplementationUnavailable before any Driver runs, and the pass resumes once the Plugin is available again

An invalid implementation fails closed: a pin of the other isolation class fails exact resolution with the same IncompatibleImplementation for either class, and a community Driver under a native pin or a release with a denied capability is refused without changing the registry

An over-budget Plugin of either isolation class (a community release over its memory budget on the real worker, or a first-party Driver over the host Tick draft budget) fails the whole pass with a typed refusal and discards the other class's staged output. Only the exhausted community Plugin is quarantined, and its release stays exhausted once cleared. The next pass within budget commits (for the community path, in a fresh lane over an in-budget successor release)

A Replay registry over a first-party Driver and a community Driver built for the real worker folds the Events a live pass of both committed into the projection the live registry folds (equal by construction: both run the same fold over the same Events), refuses to step its Drivers, steps no first-party Driver and launches no worker, and the Local and Air-Gapped passes commit and fold the same

A pass of either isolation class whose commit acknowledgement is lost is in doubt with its batch committed, and recovery returns a receipt naming exactly that batch without committing again, re-running the first-party Driver or launching a worker, and only once

A community Driver on the real worker whose probe guest proposes the host's reserved release-activation type is refused with the same ReservedHostDraft refusal and failure class as the first-party proposal of that type: the whole pass commits nothing, the first-party sibling's staged output included, no Plugin is quarantined, and the next pass commits

Invalid guest output and invalid releases fail closed: a community Driver whose guest output fails validation on the real worker fails the whole pass with InvalidGuestOutput, discards the first-party sibling's staged output and quarantines nothing, as a first-party Driver's invalid draft discards its whole pass under an authority refusal; a release whose ABI the real worker does not support and a closure whose manifest is not PMF1 are refused without changing the registry

A community release over its fuel, host-call or output budget on the real worker (one unit of fuel for the C guest; two host calls or one Event byte for the Rust guest) fails the whole pass with that typed limit and discards the first-party sibling's staged output, as a first-party Driver over the host Tick draft budget does. Only the exhausted community Plugin is quarantined (ResourceExhausted). The next pass within budget commits (for the community path, in a fresh lane over an in-budget successor release)

The ADR-119 runtime declaration refuses, before the port changes anything, a principal without the composition.fallback.declare grant, a target that is not the stepped Timeline (TargetNotStepped), DFP1 bytes that break a record rule (an oversized pin or policy, a repeated Plugin ID text), a candidate that breaks a section 4.1 rule (rule 7 over host-supplied Stable passing-profile digest sets, exact digest match) and a tenure-0 primary that is not the composer's base implementation (the runtime PrimaryNotEffective, which names the entry); the port refuses an empty first policy, StalePolicy, EntityMismatch and a primary that is not an entry's effective candidate. A byte-identical declaration retried after its commit is replayed before StalePolicy is checked

For each ADR-119 reserved type, pigloros.composition.fallback-declared and pigloros.composition.fallback-activated, a community Driver on the real worker whose probe guest drafts the type is refused with the same ReservedHostDraft refusal and failure class as the first-party draft of that type, the whole pass commits nothing and the next pass commits; a claim of the type by either class is refused with ReservedHostEventType before the registry changes

A re-base declared in a candidate tenure promotes the effective candidate: the tenure continues at chain position 0 and the new candidate is the next activation's target. A withdrawal declared in a candidate tenure freezes the effective implementation, nothing activates after it, and the next policy must name the withdrawal's digest as its predecessor (entries are tenure/chain-position/effective implementation)
